overallReasoning.summary: ZeroOps remains a single-region Azure SaaS control plane in Central India. The existing Next.js and FastAPI App Services orchestrate work while separate serverless identities analyze repositories and generate Terraform. Azure Service Bus buffers every stage, tenant-isolated Blob containers hold durable artifacts, PostgreSQL owns tenant and job metadata, and a private VM Scale Set executes only approved immutable Terraform plans.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The default test profile retains the existing B1 App Service plan and Burstable PostgreSQL server, uses Standard Service Bus, and avoids premium private-link charges where possible. The production profile enables Premium Service Bus private connectivity, P1v3 zone-redundant App Service capacity, General Purpose PostgreSQL zone-redundant HA, and private endpoints. Multi-region disaster recovery, Azure AI Search, API Management, Front Door Premium, customer-managed encryption keys, and storage-account-per-tenant isolation are deferred until scale, compliance, or measured reliability targets justify their recurring cost. The IaC module applies workload=zeroops, environment, component, owner, managedBy=terraform, dataClassification, and costCenter tags to every taggable resource; extension and child resources that do not support tags inherit cost and ownership attribution from their parent scope.

plan.validation: The approved resource topology uses Central India, where Flex Consumption and the selected PostgreSQL HA profile are available. ARM types, API versions, CAF prefixes, naming constraints, same-region dependencies, subnet delegation rules, private DNS pairings, and VMSS zone/SKU restrictions were checked. Microsoft.ServiceBus and Microsoft.App are currently not registered and, together with Microsoft.ContainerRegistry and the monitoring providers, must be registered and verified before validation. Global name availability and VM-family quota must be rechecked immediately before deployment because those subscription endpoints were unavailable during planning.
architecturePrinciples: One credential, managed identity, and blast radius per AI responsibility
Tenant ownership enforced in PostgreSQL and at every API boundary
Durable artifacts in Blob Storage; metadata and authorization in PostgreSQL
Queues carry identifiers, never source archives, secrets, or Terraform state
AI recommends; deterministic policy and human approval authorize
Scale-to-zero test defaults with explicit production reliability upgrades
Managed identity and Azure RBAC instead of shared keys
Structured observability without source code or credential leakage
Consistent ownership, environment, data-classification, and cost tags on every taggable Azure resource
